Tanker hull breach.requires: a vessel casualty at sea or in port
Tanker hull breach.provides: a finite cargo volume, a known location, release stopping when the tank empties

Offshore wellhead blowout.requires: loss of well control at the seabed
Offshore wellhead blowout.provides: continuous release for weeks, subsea origin, gas and oil together

Pipeline rupture onshore.requires: a buried or surface line failing
Pipeline rupture onshore.provides: release into land and watercourses, isolatable by valves, no marine origin

Refinery storage tank failure.provides: release inside a bunded industrial site, contained by design, no open water origin

Light crude.provides: high evaporation, spreads thinly, amenable to dispersant, brief window

Heavy bunker fuel.provides: little evaporation, persistent, sinks or tar-balls, defeats dispersant

Refined diesel.provides: very high evaporation, acutely toxic, largely gone within days

Condensate.provides: almost complete evaporation within hours, explosive vapour, nothing left to recover

Mechanical boom and skimmer.requires: workable sea state and a coherent slick
Mechanical boom and skimmer.provides: physical removal, defeated by swell, no chemical input

Chemical dispersant.requires: oil that will disperse and sufficient water depth for dilution
Chemical dispersant.provides: removal from the surface into the water column, ineffective on persistent heavy oil

In-situ burning.requires: a thick fresh slick and containment, away from population
In-situ burning.provides: rapid volume removal, air quality impact, unusable near people

Shoreline manual cleanup.requires: oil already stranded on a shore
Shoreline manual cleanup.provides: slow labour-intensive removal, no offshore application

Open sea.provides: dilution volume, room for aerial application, no immediate receptor

Enclosed harbour.provides: containment by geometry, shallow water, adjacent population

River and wetland.provides: high ecological sensitivity, no dilution depth, difficult access

Rocky shoreline.provides: complex surfaces retaining oil, no vessel access

Calm.provides: workable conditions for all offshore techniques

Moderate swell.provides: boom performance degraded, aerial application still possible

Storm conditions.provides: no vessel operations, natural dispersion accelerated

_v1_notes.SPILL SOURCE|OIL TYPE: condensate is gas-associated, so it is Y only for a wellhead blowout and N for a tanker, a pipeline and a storage tank as posed. A blowout produces crude and condensate, not bunker fuel or refined diesel.
_v1_notes.SPILL SOURCE|RESPONSE TECHNIQUE: an onshore pipeline rupture and a refinery tank failure are both N for dispersant (no marine water column to disperse into) and N for in-situ burning near a populated industrial site.
_v1_notes.SPILL SOURCE|ENVIRONMENT: a tanker breach is N in a river and wetland. A blowout is N in a harbour and N in a river - it is a subsea event offshore. A pipeline rupture is Y only in a river and wetland. A tank failure is Y only in an enclosed harbour setting adjacent to the site.
_v1_notes.OIL TYPE|RESPONSE TECHNIQUE: condensate defeats every technique - it evaporates within hours, leaving nothing to boom, disperse, burn or clean. Heavy bunker fuel defeats dispersant and burning. Diesel is N for in-situ burning, evaporating faster than a burn can be organised.
_v1_notes.OIL TYPE|ENVIRONMENT: condensate is N in a river and wetland and N on a rocky shoreline - it does not persist to strand.
_v1_notes.RESPONSE TECHNIQUE|ENVIRONMENT: boom and skimmer are N in a river and wetland and N on a rocky shoreline - no vessel access. Dispersant needs dilution depth so it is N everywhere except open sea. In-situ burning is N except open sea, being unusable near people or vegetation. Shoreline cleanup is N at open sea.
_v1_notes.RESPONSE TECHNIQUE|SEA STATE: boom, dispersant and burning are all N in storm conditions - no vessel or aerial operations. Burning is also N in moderate swell, which breaks up the thick slick it requires.
